 IRS provides dyed diesel fuel relief related to excise tax following President Trump’s Executive Order
 
 



 
IR-2026-122, Oct. 14, 2026 — The Internal Revenue Service today announced that, in response to the President’s Oct. 5, 2026, Executive Order, Emergency Tax Relief on Diesel Fuel, it will not impose a penalty when dyed diesel fuel is sold for use or used on highways nationwide.
 
 



 

 
 Treasury and IRS move to protect health care benefits for eligible Americans
 
 



 
IR-2026-121, Oct. 14, 2026 — The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service issued proposed regulations to implement President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts reforms to the Premium Tax Credit (PTC), a refundable tax credit that helps eligible American taxpayers afford health insurance purchased through the Health Insurance Exchanges.
 
 



 

 
 IRS highlights partnership with UK tax authority’s new whistleblower program
 
 



 
IR-2026-120, Oct. 7, 2026 — The Internal Revenue Service today highlighted its partnership with the United Kingdom’s whistleblower program, which drew upon the IRS Whistleblower Office’s expertise to quickly get established.
 
 



 

 
 IRS reminder: Cybersecurity Awareness Month offers simple steps to protect tax data 
 
 



 
IR-2026-119, Oct. 2, 2026 — The Internal Revenue Service today encouraged taxpayers to take simple steps to strengthen online security during Cybersecurity Awareness Month.
 

 
 



 

 
 The IRS seeks community partners and volunteers to support free tax services
 
 



 
IR-2026-118, Oct. 1, 2026 — The Internal Revenue Service’s Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) and Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE) programs are seeking volunteers and community partners to help provide free tax preparation services during the upcoming filing season. 
 
 



 

 
 The Trump administration advances the establishment of America’s first nationwide school choice program
 
 



 
IR-2026-117, Oct. 1, 2026 — The Department of the Treasury and the IRS issued proposed regulations to implement the new Federal Scholarship Tax Credit under section 25F, commonly known as the Education Freedom Tax Credit, the first federal tax credit supporting private contributions for K-12 scholarships.
